data.title: Prefers Reduced Motion
data.tagline: Reading the system's reduce motion setting and disabling or reducing animation accordingly
data.learningOutcome: You can toggle the system preference and check that the page reduces nonessential motion while keeping its state clear.
data.description: When visitors enable their system's reduced-motion preference, a page can query it and reduce, stop, or replace nonessential animation, such as replacing a large movement with a static state. Keep loading and status information clear; a spinning icon can be replaced with text or progress. Toggle the system setting to check that the page responds.

learning.assumes: You have seen page animations, or heard of the system's reduce motion setting.
learning.outcome: You can toggle the system preference and check that the page reduces nonessential motion while keeping its state clear.

distinctions.label: Pause button
distinctions.explanation: A pause button lets users control playback manually; reduce motion reads the system setting and reduces automatically—different triggers.

distinctions.label: Loading state
distinctions.explanation: Reduced motion can also stop a loading spinner; keep a static text or progress cue so users still know the page is waiting. Preserving the information does not require preserving the animation.

explanation.title: Nonessential animation can change
explanation.text: When the preference is on, reduce, stop, or replace nonessential motion such as large movement or parallax.

explanation.title: Keep the page state clear
explanation.text: You can stop a loading spinner and use text or progress to show that work continues; keeping the information does not require keeping the animation.

explanation.title: Verify with the system setting
explanation.text: After changing it, toggle the system setting once and check whether the page animation actually follows—that is acceptance.

data.boundary: Reduced motion expresses a preference for less nonessential movement; an implementation can reduce, stop, or replace animation. Whatever the choice, keep the page state clear.

lessonPractice.title: An accessibility check flags that the page does not respond to the system's reduce motion setting. What should happen next?

options.label: Respond to the system preference, reduce nonessential motion, and keep the page state clear
options.feedback: Correct. A loading spinner can stop, but the page should still show that it is waiting. Toggle the preference to confirm the page responds.

options.label: Add a pause button to every animation
options.feedback: Buttons require users to find and click them; the system setting already expresses the preference and the page should respond automatically.

options.label: Delete the loading message and status information too
options.feedback: The spinner can stop, but the loading and status information should remain. Use static text or progress to show that the page is still waiting.

data.agentPrompt: Make the page respond to the system's reduced-motion preference by reducing or replacing nonessential animation. A loading spinner may stop, but keep static text or progress feedback so the waiting state is clear. Toggle the system setting to verify the page responds.
